body:
ADR checkpoint reviewed; implementation starting

I accept the final division and checkpoint. The first Intaglio work product is now at docs/reviews/2026-08-28-intaglio-gap-evaluation.md under bd-01M14K85783PMTBFP8GJYXMQDJ. It records exact Intaglio SHA 596b398, a clean checkout, coreJVM 221/221 and svgJVM 24/24 focused tests, a capability matrix, responsibility boundary, WOG tracer laws, and benchmark plan.

Key result: no Intaglio change is needed for the first SVG tracer or Codex overlay. Existing Viewport is enough for the first pan/zoom camera lowering and SVG already preserves GraphicsName as data-name. Generic gaps are later Canvas bounds/hit testing, scalar fields with a coverage mask, and perhaps native curves after tessellation is measured.

Two ADR type-shape corrections surfaced before view implementation:

1. Section 6 says GraphicsName is derived from Address. One Address can produce several annotations, placed fragments, and Atlas marks, so Address alone is not injective within one rendered artifact. GraphicsName should derive from the rendered mark or fragment identity; NavigationIndex maps that marker many-to-one back to Address. Semantic selection remains Set[Address]. I will keep marker identity out of the portable CodexFlow foundation.

2. TextAnnotation.status: EpistemicStatus is not total for feature observations, missing estimates, raw versus calibrated values, resolution alternatives, unresolved states, or align exclusions. The base annotation should not force those into a claim status. I propose TextAnnotation carries target Address plus AuditRecord, and domain state is resolved from the addressed object. If a cached display state is later needed, it must be a checked typed sum covering D9, not EpistemicStatus. I will omit the universal status field in the foundation rather than silently misclassify non-claim annotations.

Everything else in sections 3 to 4 is implementable as written. I am preflighting build.sbt and view/** now. Please object promptly if either correction is not what you intended; I will keep them isolated and visible in tests.
